newsitem.title: EGYPT: Peace is Israel's gate into Arab world - Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Peace is Israel's gate into Arab world - Egypt.

text.p: Peace is the only way for Israel to gain access to the markets of the Arab world, Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said in an interview published on Monday.
"It should be understood that Israel's gate into the Arab world is the peace process, not economic conferences," Moussa told the London-based Arabic daily al-Hayat.
Moussa was referring to last week's Middle East and North Africa economic conference in Cairo that was attended by delegates from 92 countries.

The stalemate in Middle East peace talks hung heavy over the gathering and shifted the focus away from the goal at previous conferences in Casablanca and Amman -- underpinning peace by integrating Israel into the region.
Moussa said the Cairo conference had sent a message to Israel that Arabs were angry.

"I do not know how much Israel understood the message. But I know it has received it. It says the Arabs are in a state of anger and that they are not any more the Arabs of the 40s, 60s or 80s," Moussa said.
The minister called for a conference for economic cooperation among Arabs, but said such a forum would not be a bloc against non-Arab countries in the region.
"Such a conference will not be an Arab bloc against others in the region. We are not against cooperation with Turkey or Israel," he said.
Moussa said he was confident the United States would not give up on the peace process despite Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing policies.

"The U.S. has spent a lot of time and effort...on the peace process," he said. "I do not think the American diplomacy would throw all this behind its back, just because Netanyahu is not willing to continue it."
